title: Partial Indexes in PostgreSQL
realWorldScenario: A job queue table has 10 million completed jobs and 500 pending jobs. Workers frequently run: `SELECT * FROM jobs WHERE status = 'PENDING' ORDER BY priority DESC;`
questionStatement: What is a Partial Index in PostgreSQL? Write the DDL to index only pending jobs. Why is this superior to a full table index?
expectedConcepts: Drastic reduction in index size and disk footprint
Zero write overhead for non-matching rows
hints: Add a WHERE clause directly to CREATE INDEX.
